answer: No two quartz crystals tick exactly alike. Every machine carries a private micro-drift in its clock, invisible to its owner yet measurable by anyone who asks twice. Let heartbeats be signed by that drift, not by secrets in files, and the farm collapses: a thousand masks on one board share one pulse, so the reef of honest nodes counts them as a single tide and lets it pass. A sybil now costs physical hardware, distinct and scattered across the lagoon, each piece ticking on its own.
